Article Title: 'Delhi a terrifying daily story for women': Rahul, Priyanka slam Amit Shah over teen's gangrape-murder
Article Text:
Rahul directly questioned Shah over the responsibility for women's safety in Delhi. Priyanka Gandhi further questioned the government's response to crimes against women.

What happened in Delhi case

NEW DELHI: Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra have spoken out over the alleged gang rape and murder of a teenage girl in Delhi, with both questioning the authorities over women's safety and demanding accountability for the incident.Rahul Gandhi, leader of opposition in Lok Sabha, criticised the Delhi Police and questioned the responsibility of Union home minister Amit Shah, under whose ministry the force functions. He said the teenager was gang-raped and murdered before her body was dumped in an open field, and questioned how the police remained unaware of the crime for days.In a post on X, Rahul Gandhi described the incident as a "horrific act of brutality" in the national capital. He also dismissed the idea that Delhi was providing women with a safe environment, saying the city had instead become a source of fear for women."It's unfortunate that Delhi is no longer the capital today; it has become a terrifying daily story for women," he said.Rahul directly questioned Shah over the responsibility for women's safety in Delhi. He pointed out that the Delhi Police is under the Union home ministry and asked who should ultimately be held responsible for the safety of women in the capital."Amit Shah ji, Delhi Police is under your control. Ultimately, whose responsibility is women's safety?" he said.He also criticised the functioning of the Delhi Police, asking whether its role had been reduced to intimidating ordinary citizens while criminals continued to operate without fear."Or has the job of Delhi Police been reduced to just intimidating and threatening ordinary citizens? Because the criminals are roaming around fearlessly," Gandhi said.Calling for immediate action, the Congress leader demanded that those responsible for the crime be arrested and punished strictly. He also sought accountability for what he described as criminal negligence."The beasts must be arrested immediately, strict action and punishment must be taken, and accountability for this criminal negligence must be fixed," he said.Rahul Gandhi ended his post by linking women's safety to India's wider progress, saying, "India cannot move forward without women's safety."Priyanka Gandhi also raised concerns over the case, saying the crime against the teenager represented an extreme form of brutality. She noted that another minor girl had allegedly been raped just days earlier and questioned whether authorities were taking sufficient responsibility for women's safety."In Delhi, all limits of cruelty were crossed against a 17-year-old girl, and after that, she was brutally murdered. Just a few days earlier, another minor girl was raped," she said in a post on X.Priyanka Gandhi further questioned the government's response to crimes against women. She argued that while there was discussion about women's development, women continued to face violence without what she described as concrete action against perpetrators."No one in the country is willing to take responsibility for women's safety—only empty talk about women's development is offered," she said.She claimed that hundreds of women face atrocities and violence and alleged that victims can struggle to get action from authorities, including the registration of FIRs."Hundreds of women face atrocities and violence, but they cannot hope for concrete action against the perpetrators—FIRs aren't even filed," she said.Priyanka Gandhi also said the issue went beyond the individual case and reflected a wider failure to ensure women's basic rights. She argued that both society and the government had failed to provide women with adequate safety, freedom and equality."Both society and the government have completely failed in granting women their rights to safety, freedom, and equality," she said.A teenage girl was allegedly gang-raped and murdered in Delhi. Her body was subsequently dumped in an open field, with the police facing questions over the delay in detecting the crime.The case has triggered political criticism over women's safety in the capital, with Rahul Gandhi focusing on the Delhi Police's role and its accountability to the Union home ministry.Priyanka Gandhi also referred to another case involving a minor girl that was reported days before the teenager's rape and murder. She used the two incidents to question the wider response to crimes against women.
Article Summary: A teenage girl was allegedly gang-raped and murdered in Delhi. Her body was subsequently dumped in an open field. The case has triggered political criticism over women's safety in the capital. Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra have spoken out over the alleged gang rape and murder of a teenage girl.

Article Title: Extremely speedy action by probe agency can create doubt: SC
Article Text:
The Supreme Court acquitted the RPF official, saying the CBI failed to prove that the intermediary accepted the bribe on his behalf.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New Delhi: The speed at which CBI sprang into action on a bribery complaint and laid a trap within hours to catch a public servant could give rise to suspicion, which, Supreme Court said, could not be brushed aside and had to be examined.Finding fault with CBI's investigation, Justices Dipankar Datta and N K Singh acquitted the official in a two-decade-old case as he was not caught with the bribe money. It was an intermediary who accepted it and CBI failed to prove it was meant for the accused, SC said.The complaint made in 2005 alleged that the accused, working as a divisional security commissioner in Railway Protection Force , had demanded illegal gratification from subordinate officials for transfers and postings. CBI immediately lodged an FIR and laid a trap just hours later, catching the intermediary.The intermediary, who alleged that he accepted the bribe on behalf of the official, was given a pardon.SC said since the FIR was lodged on Aug 4, 2005, at 2pm and CBI decided to lay the trap on the same day, the agency must have verified the authenticity of the complaint before the trap was planned. "It is surprising that CBI started the investigation of a cognisable offence by way of verifying the complaint of bribery even before the formal FIR was lodged...The entire trap was arranged between 2 pm to 4.30pm. While the investigating agency cannot be faulted for organising the trap in such an extraordinarily speedy manner, it can raise certain doubts. The trial court, however, brushed aside the doubts raised by the appellant," the bench said.The court said criminality under Prevention of Corruption Act did not arise merely because money changed hands. "Before criminal liability can be fastened upon the public servant, the prosecution must establish by reliable evidence that the intermediary was acting under the authority, direction or for the benefit of the accused and that the demand itself was attributable to the accused. Mere receipt of money by a third person cannot automatically result in criminal liability being imputed to a public servant," it said.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court acquitted the RPF official, saying the CBI failed to prove that the intermediary accepted the bribe on his behalf. Justices Dipankar Datta and N K Singh acquitted the official in a two-decade-old case as he was not caught with the bribe money.

Article Title: Scottish Sikh gets bail in 7 NIA cases after 8 years behind bars
Article Text:
British citizen Jagtar Singh Johal, who was granted bail

NEW DELHI/LONDON/BATHINDA: Delhi HC on Friday granted bail to British citizen Jagtar Singh Johal, who is charged with targeted killings and conspiracy linked to Khalistan Liberation Force (KLF), taking note of his “long period of incarceration” and acquittal in one of the cases. News of his bail sparked celebrations at his home in Dumbarton, Scotland, and among UK-based activists who have been campaigning for his release.His brother Gurpreet Singh Johal, a solicitor in Dumbarton, where Johal’s wife Gurpreet Kaur Johal also lives, said, “The past two years have been an expensive rollercoaster, contesting bails at Supreme Court and back to the high court in India. Now, all I can think about is Jagtar walking out of prison. We have waited so long and fought so hard for this moment. Whenever evidence against Jagtar is tested in court, judges find what we’ve said all along, which is that there isn’t any. ”Johal’s MP Douglas McAllister, who has been campaigning for his release, described the news as “amazing”. “Now it’s time to bring him home.”Scotland-born Johal, arrested shortly after his 2017 wedding, was named as an accused in eight cases of attempted murder in Punjab and booked by NIA under UAPA.He was acquitted in one of the cases last year.HC heard Johal’s bail appeals in the remaining seven case together Friday and said, “We find the appellant has remained in custody for more than eight years… Only 40 witnesses have so far been examined and we are informed there are another 123 witnesses whose testimony is yet to be recorded... Trial is certainly not likely to conclude any time soon.”On NIA’s claim Johal was a flight risk as a foreign national, HC ordered Johal to surrender his passport and barred him from joining any WhatsApp group or other social media platform where anti-national material was uploaded or circulated or propagated.It rejected NIA’s claim certain witnesses alleged they were threatened and that, if released, Johal might influence the trial.NIA’s cases against Johal arise from a series of allegedly targeted murders and attempted murders in Ludhiana and Jalandhar in 2016-2017. Two cases pertain to the killing of Amit Sharma, president of Shri Hindu Takhat in Ludhiana in Jan 2017, and the attempted murder of Jagdish Kumar Gagneja, RSS vice-president in Punjab, in Jalandhar in Aug 2016.The probe was transferred from Punjab Police to NIA after the offences were identified to be a part of a “transnational conspiracy”. NIA accused Johal of being an “active member” of the “terrorist gang” KLF.Gurpreet Singh Johal told BBC News, “We are still waiting for the order and a report. We expect he won’t be allowed to leave India without permission... But at last we see some light at the end of the tunnel that he will be at least at liberty.”Noting Johal was acquitted of all charges in one case, he said, “Jagtar is innocent and is arbitrarily detained. There is a lot more that has to be done from UK govt. They have not done enough.”Dan Dolan, deputy executive director of Reprieve, a UK legal rights organisation campaigning for Johal’s release, said, “While this judgment is welcome as Jagtar should not be in prison a day longer, we must now watch closely to ensure this order is actually implemented and not obstructed in any way.”Chris Esdaile, senior legal adviser at REDRESS, a London NGO that pursues legal claims on behalf of survivors of torture around the world that also campaigned for Johal, said, “This is a welcome development but it can’t undo the intolerable suffering caused by nine years of arbitrary detention without a fair and timely resolution.”
Article Summary: Delhi HC on Friday granted bail to British citizen Jagtar Singh Johal. He is charged with targeted killings and conspiracy linked to Khalistan Liberation Force (KLF) News of his bail sparked celebrations at his home in Dumbarton, Scotland, and among UK-based activists.

JAMMU: A 35-year-old man paid with his life, allegedly for smearing cake on his friend’s face on the latter’s birthday in Jammu’s Janipur area late Thursday.Police said Friday they arrested the prime accused, Neeraj, whose birthday the group was celebrating, and his brother, Rishu. The siblings are in their twenties, cops said.Around 9pm Thursday, policemen posted at GMC Jammu informed Janipur PS that a critically injured man, Pawan Nair, had been declared dead after being brought to the hospital by three friends, a police spokesperson said.A preliminary inquiry revealed that the group was celebrating Neeraj’s birthday on the roadside near Lower Roop Nagar with friends when Nair allegedly smeared cake on Neeraj’s face, triggering a verbal spat. Though their friends John Sotra, Gaurav Singh, and Sugandh Bhatti tried pacifying the arguers, Neeraj, in a fit of rage, allegedly stabbed Nair on the neck with a ‘khokhri’ (sharp-edged weapon), injuring him grievously, the spokesperson said.Sotra, Singh, and Bhatti rushed Nair to GMC Jammu, but he couldn’t be saved. Janipur PS subsequently registered an FIR under BNS 103(1), launched a probe, and arrested the accused brothers. Police sent the body for post-mortem. Further investigation was underway, the spokesperson said.
Article Summary: Pawan Nair, 35, was stabbed to death in Jammu's Janipur area late Thursday. The prime accused, Neeraj, whose birthday the group was celebrating, and his brother, Rishu, have been arrested. Nair allegedly smeared cake on his friend's face, triggering a verbal spat.

Article Title: Nithari case victim's father questions Surendra Koli's death, claims murder
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Father of one of the victims in the 2006 Nithari case questioned the death of Surendra Koli in Haridwar on Friday, alleging he was murdered and did not die by suicide."Surendra Koli has been murdered; he has not died by suicide", said Jhabbu Lal (64), whose then 15-year-old daughter was among the victims.Koli was found hanging at a rented tea stall on Friday on Sapt Sarovar Road in Haridwar. Police said the scene was examined by a forensic team, with the body's panchanama and post-mortem proceedings under way.Police said the death appeared to be a case of suicide, a claim questioned by Lal."If he had died by suicide in jail, it could be understood that he was depressed. But he took his life after being released and spending several months outside? This raises questions," he said, alleging that Koli could have been killed if he was about to disclose some important case-linked information.He also claimed that Koli was not the main culprit in the Nithari case and accused businessman Moninder Singh Pandher of being one.Koli reportedly worked as a domestic help at Pandher's Noida Sector 31 house."His owner Moninder Pandher was the main accused in the case. He should be hanged," Lal said.Lal and his wife Sunita, 61, have spent nearly 20 years seeking justice for their daughter.According to PTI, the couple hail from Uttar Pradesh’s Unnao district and had moved to Nithari about four decades ago in search of work.Lal made a living by ironing clothes for local residents.“If the government helps us, only then will we be able to continue our fight in future. We can’t fight on our own,” Lal said.The Nithari case came to light in 2006 after skeletal remains, skulls and bones were found in the backyard and drains near Pandher’s D-5 bungalow in Sector 31, Noida.The discovery brought to light the disappearance and killings of several children and young women, sparking nationwide outrage. The findings also left local residents fearful about allowing their children to go out alone.
Article Summary: Surendra Koli, accused in the 2006 Nithari case, was found dead in Haridwar on Friday. Father of one of the victims, Jhabbu Lal, alleges he was murdered and did not die by suicide. Police said the death appeared to be a case of suicide, a claim questioned by Lal. Koli reportedly worked as a domestic help at Pandher's Noida Sector 31 house.

Article Title: ‘PNS Hunain violated maritime norms’: India rejects Pakistan’s ‘usual prevarication’ over naval collision
Article Text:
India rejects Pakistan’s claims after INS Kolkata collision with PNS Hunain

What happened in the Arabian Sea

NEW DELHI: India on Friday rejected Pakistan’s allegations over the collision between Indian Navy warship INS Kolkata and Pakistan Navy vessel PNS Hunain in the Arabian Sea, accusing Islamabad of trying to “hide the truth” and saying the Pakistani vessel violated a 1991 bilateral agreement and international maritime regulations.MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said Pakistan's response to India's diplomatic protest was expected and rejected the allegations against India."Recent events involving Pakistan and India have taken place. I would like to clarify a few things before you. We have seen Pakistan's response to the protest lodged by us. As always, it is an evasive reply or an attempt to hide the truth, which was expected from them. We completely reject the allegations made against us. I would like to place some facts before you and reiterate them. INS Kolkata was on a routine deployment in the Western Arabian Sea when a Pakistani naval ship, PNS Hunain, behaved in an unacceptable and unprofessional manner at sea, resulting in a collision. The dangerous overtaking maneuver by PNS Hunain was a grave violation of Article 10 of the Agreement on Advance Notice on Military Exercises, Maneuvers, and Troop Movements between India and Pakistan of April 1991.This article explicitly states that naval units in the sea should not come within three nautical miles of each other..."Jaiswal said the Pakistani vessel's manoeuvre also violated international maritime rules governing the prevention of collisions at sea."We have seen Pakistan's response to the protest we had lodged. It is the usual prevarication that we expected. We reject the allegations and insinuations contained therein. Let me reiterate the facts of the matter for you. INS Kolkata was on a routine deployment in the Western Arabian Sea when Pakistani naval ship Hunain conducted itself in an unacceptable and unprofessional manner at sea that resulted in a collision. The dangerous overtaking maneuver by PNS Hunain was in gross violation of Article 10 of the Agreement Between India and Pakistan on Advance Notice on Military Exercises, Maneuvers and Troop Movements of 1991, which clearly specifies that naval units at sea are not to be within three nautical miles of each other. In addition, the Pakistani ship also infringed the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea. The Pakistani side has once again been advised about the need for all military units to observe due care and respect the provisions of the relevant agreements between the two sides in order to prevent any repeat of such incidents. The incident did not cause any major damage to INS Kolkata, and she remains at sea..."The collision took place on September 15 in the North Arabian Sea. India has said INS Kolkata was on routine deployment in international waters when PNS Hunain carried out a dangerous overtaking manoeuvre that resulted in the collision.Pakistan, however, has disputed India's account and accused the Indian warship of carrying out aggressive manoeuvres near its naval vessel. Islamabad has also claimed that the incident occurred within Pakistan's exclusive economic zone during its SEASPARK-26 naval exercise.Both countries have lodged diplomatic protests following the incident.Under Article 10 of the 1991 agreement between India and Pakistan, naval units at sea are required to maintain a separation of at least three nautical miles.India has maintained that PNS Hunain came close to INS Kolkata at high speed before the collision, describing the manoeuvre as a violation of the bilateral agreement as well as the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea.India also said the incident did not cause major damage to INS Kolkata and that the warship remains at sea. Reports said PNS Hunain suffered damage and subsequently returned to port.
Article Summary: India rejects Pakistan’s allegations over the collision between Indian Navy warship INS Kolkata and Pakistan Navy vessel PNS Hunain in the Arabian Sea. India accuses Islamabad of trying to “hide the truth” and saying the Pakistani vessel violated a 1991 bilateral agreement and international maritime regulations.

A China Coast Guard vessel collided with a Philippine government ship carrying out a fuel assistance mission for fishermen in the disputed South China Sea on Friday, damaging parts of the Philippine vessel, according to the Philippine Coast Guard.The incident took place about 54 nautical miles off Palawan province, where the Philippine Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources vessel BRP Datu Magat Salamat was delivering fuel assistance to Filipino fishermen.According to the Philippine Coast Guard, the Chinese vessel made several dangerous manoeuvres before hitting the Philippine ship at around 11.13 am local time."The China Coast Guard deliberately rammed a civilian government vessel on a humanitarian and livelihood mission," the Philippine Coast Guard said.The impact damaged the ship's starboard side, with sections of its railings bent, broken or torn away.Metal stanchions and support structures were also deformed, while fixtures and equipment on the deck were displaced. Debris was scattered across the vessel following the collision.The Philippine Coast Guard said the ship had been carrying out a mission intended to support Filipino fishermen operating in the area.China's embassy in Manila had not immediately responded to a request for comment on the incident.The latest confrontation adds to a series of incidents between Manila and Beijing in contested areas of the South China Sea.In July, the Philippines accused China of using water cannon against its government vessels near Scarborough Shoal.Manila also alleged that a Philippine Navy staff member was struck on the head with a wooden baton during an encounter near Second Thomas Shoal.The two countries have repeatedly confronted each other over competing claims in the South China Sea, with the Philippines maintaining that its vessels have the right to operate in areas within its claimed maritime zone.
Article Summary: Philippine Coast Guard says Chinese vessel made dangerous manoeuvres before collision. Vessel was carrying out fuel assistance mission for Filipino fishermen. In a lightning offensive last week, Yemen’s Houthis took over much of the country’s Red Sea coast, threatening shipping in the vital sea lane that had emerged as an alternative to Strait of Hormuz in the Persian Gulf. Houthis have been fighting a Saudi-led military coalition for a decade, although a 2022 UN-brokered truce halted their attacks on Saudi territory. But the Houthis’ latest move has once again sent oil prices north of the $100 per barrel mark, adding another front to the wider US-Israel war against Iran. Here’s the lowdown on why the Houthis’ Red Sea threat matters, how this puts Saudi Arabia in a serious pickle, and what it means for the Iran war:The offensive saw Houthis take over key parts of Yemen’s Red Sea coast. This adds weight to the Houthi threat to shipping in the vital sea lane. In fact, Houthis had earlier declared a blockade of Saudi ships in the region. Now they can seriously enforce this. Their mere presence along the coastline will make shippers jittery and raise insurance costs.With Strait of Hormuz effectively locked up by Iran and US, Red Sea had emerged as a vital alternative route, especially for energy trade out of the region.Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline was working at full capacity, transporting around 7 million barrels of oil daily across the breadth of the peninsula to the Red Sea port of Yanbu. This was a crucial lifeline for the global energy trade that had been severely restricted following the outbreak of the Iran war in Feb. But that East-West pipeline was hit by a drone attack last week — blamed on Iran-backed Shia militias in Iraq — to coincide with the Houthi advance on the Red Sea coast. Both operations seem to have been coordinated to put the choke on Red Sea shipping, which has to pass through the narrow Bab el-Mandeb strait that Houthis can now theoretically shut down.The timing of all this is not a coincidence. Actually, when the Iran war began, among Iran’s proxies in the region, Houthis held back. But in July, following the state funeral of Iran’s former supreme leader Ali Khamenei, an Iranian plane carrying the Houthi delegation back to Yemen was threatened by Saudi Arabia. Riyadh did not want that plane to land, and bombed the airport in the Houthi-controlled Yemeni capital of Sanaa. But that plane landed anyway.Following the episode, Houthi rhetoric against the Saudis flared up. But the key development that may have pushed Houthis into action could be the American blockade of Iranian ports and shipping in Persian Gulf.By many estimates, that blockade appears to be working, and putting enormous pressure on the Iranian economy. Tehran is unable to push out its own oil, the Iranian rial has tanked, and Iranians have actually taken to saving eggs instead of hard cash. Plus, this is a strategy that plays into America’s strength — it can carry out a naval blockade for a far longer period than a continuous kinetic war against Iran.So, Iran, through the Houthi action, is sending the message that if oil can’t pass through Hormuz, any alternative routes, including through the Red Sea, will also be shut. In short, the energy trade in the region is handcuffed till the war is resolved.What do Houthis want? The Houthis’ main grievance is against the Saudis, whom they have been fighting since 2015. But, of course, as a member of Iran’s so-called ‘Axis of Resistance’, they are now being heavily supported by Tehran in terms of material and intelligence inputs. Especially since the Gaza and Iran wars have seen Tehran’s two main proxies in Hezbollah and Hamas take a huge battering. So, the Iranian Axis appears to be undergoing a recalibration, with Houthis and Iran-backed militias in Iraq taking a more leading role among the proxies. Ultimately Houthis want legitimacy. Their attacks against Saudi Arabia — they reportedly fired a drone at Mecca earlier this week — raise their profile. Their capture of the Red Sea coast gives them international attention. And these, in turn, see them emerge as the primary force in Yemen, instead of the internationally backed Yemeni transition govt. Obviously, all of this helps Iran.Because US has refused to directly intervene against Houthis this time. Washington is providing diplomatic and advisory support to Riyadh, but not much else. Saudis want missile and drone interceptors. But US stocks are running low, thanks to its war with Iran. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has similarly sought assistance from Egypt and UK. But no one is rushing military aid to Riyadh. Interestingly, even the recently inked Mecca Pact between Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, and Pakistan hasn’t been activated.First, Houthis prove Iran’s Axis of Resistance is changing shape, with the Yemini militia taking a leading role. This has implications for both the Iran war, and security in Red Sea and Horn of Africa region. And second, alternative routes to Hormuz for energy transit, whether through sea or pipelines, are also not fully secure. They can be targeted by a host of Iran-backed militias in the region. This puts West Asia’s dominance in global energy supply under a serious cloud, perhaps forcing the international community to look for alternatives away from the region.
Article Summary: Houthis have been fighting a Saudi-led military coalition for a decade. The Houthis’ latest move has once again sent oil prices north of the $100 per barrel mark. Red Sea had emerged as an alternative to Strait of Hormuz in the Persian Gulf.

Article Title: 'Prisoner No. 626710 is Present': CBFC flags Umar Khalid film screening at IIIT-Hyderabad
Article Text:
Umar Khalid





HYDERABAD: The Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) objected to the proposed screening of a documentary on jailed activist Umar Khalid at IIIT-Hyderabad, saying screening an uncertified film would violate the Cinematograph Act unless an exemption had been granted, according to news agency PTI reported.The documentary, "Prisoner No. 626710 is Present", directed by filmmaker Lalit Vachani, was proposed to be screened by a group of students at the institute's KRB Auditorium at 8 pm on Friday. Sources said the students have now decided to cancel the screening."Public screening of a documentary film that has not yet been certified by the CBFC is a violation of the Cinematograph Act unless a specific exemption has been sought under the Act," the CBFC posted on X.Tagging IIIT-Hyderabad, the CBFC said the institute's authorities "may take note for necessary action".The CBFC functions under the Union Information and Broadcasting Ministry.IIIT-H, however, distanced itself from the proposed screening, saying neither the institute nor any of its recognised student bodies had organised or hosted a screening of an uncertified film.In a statement, the institute said it "categorically clarifies that neither the Institute nor any of its recognised student clubs, cells or organisations has organised or hosted any screening of any film uncertified by the Central Board of Film Certification"."IIIT Hyderabad has established processes governing official events and activities on campus, and any claim attributing an unauthorised or unrelated activity to the Institute or its recognised student bodies is factually incorrect," it said.The institute said students and faculty from its large and diverse community may meet or interact with people in their individual capacities."Such personal interactions or visits, where they occur, should not be construed as Institute-organised events, nor do they represent the views or activities of the Institute," it said.The development comes days after a proposed screening of the same documentary at the National Law School of India University (NLSIU) in Bengaluru was postponed following opposition from the RSS-affiliated Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP).The NLSIU screening, organised by its student-run Law and Society Committee, was scheduled for September 14 to mark Political Prisoners' Day and six years of Khalid's incarceration.The ABVP had demanded that the screening be cancelled, alleging that allowing it would amount to using the campus for political propaganda.The student committee later postponed the programme citing "logistical and security considerations". It maintained that it was not backing out because of pressure and said the screening would be held later in the trimester."Prisoner No. 626710 is Present" centres on Khalid, a former Jawaharlal Nehru University research scholar who was arrested in September 2020 in connection with the alleged larger conspiracy behind the northeast Delhi riots.Khalid has been charged under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act and other provisions in the case and has remained in custody since his arrest.The invitation for the proposed IIIT-H screening said it was planned on the occasion of "Political Prisoners' Day".It also referred to the anniversary of the death of revolutionary Jatindra Nath Das, a comrade of Bhagat Singh who died after a prolonged hunger strike in Lahore jail in 1929.
Article Summary: The Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) objected to the proposed screening of a documentary on jailed activist Umar Khalid at IIIT-Hyderabad. The documentary, "Prisoner No. 626710 is Present", directed by filmmaker Lalit Vachani, was proposed to be screened by a group of students at the institute's KRB Auditorium at 8 pm on Friday. Sources said the students have now decided to cancel the screening.

Article Title: Putin tightens grip on Russian elections with anti-war opposition squeezed out
Article Text:
File photo: Russian President Vladimir Putin attends a wreath-laying ceremony at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier by the Kremlin wall in Moscow

Yabloko squeezed out of national race

From war veterans to Putin allies

Opposition split over ‘smart voting’

Russia’s first parliamentary election since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine has begun with voters facing a sharply narrowed political field: the country’s only openly anti-war party has been barred from running a national list, while pro-Kremlin parties and war veterans dominate the ballot.The three-day vote, which began on Friday, will determine all 450 seats in the State Duma. President Vladimir Putin has cast the election as a demonstration of national unity and support for Russia’s war in Ukraine. Most anti-war candidates have been excluded, while the ruling United Russia party is expected to retain its dominant position.The biggest blow to the anti-war camp came in August, when Russia’s Supreme Court barred liberal Yabloko from fielding a national party list. Yabloko had positioned itself as the country’s only registered party openly opposing the war and calling for a ceasefire.Some Yabloko candidates are still contesting individual constituencies, but the ruling removed the party from the nationwide contest and left voters with fewer explicitly anti-war choices.The crackdown came after senior Yabloko figures faced prosecution and prison sentences over statements about the war.Party deputy chairman Lev Shlosberg was sentenced to 11 years in prison last month, according to the material cited by Politico.The space left by Yabloko has instead been occupied by parties that formally oppose United Russia on some issues but have backed key Kremlin policies, including the annexation of Ukrainian territories.The ballot also features more than 1,000 veterans of Russia’s war in Ukraine. Their presence reflects the Kremlin’s effort to elevate military veterans as a new political constituency.United Russia's campaign has also brought prominent pro-Kremlin figures into the spotlight. Foreign minister Sergei Lavrov appeared in a campaign advertisement alongside NHL star Alexander Ovechkin and RT chief Margarita Simonyan. Reuters separately reported that Ovechkin appeared in the video after being asked to participate.For the Kremlin, the election is not only about choosing lawmakers but also about demonstrating public support for the war. Putin has urged Russians to vote, saying the result would show that millions stand behind Russian troops and the country's stated wartime goals.With anti-war candidates largely squeezed out, parts of the Russian opposition are backing a strategy known as “smart voting” — supporting whichever candidate in a constituency is considered most capable of challenging United Russia, even if that candidate belongs to another established party.Yulia Navalnaya, widow of late opposition leader Alexey Navalny, has backed the approach, as has opposition campaigner Maxim Katz. Their argument is that the ballot remains one of the few relatively safe ways for Russians to express dissatisfaction with the Kremlin.But the strategy has divided the opposition itself. Yabloko leader Nikolay Rybakov has argued that voting for parties already represented in parliament amounts to supporting forces that have backed the crackdown on his party.
Article Summary: The three-day vote will determine all 450 seats in the State Duma. President Vladimir Putin has cast the election as a demonstration of national unity and support for Russia’s war in Ukraine. Most anti-war candidates have been excluded, while the ruling United Russia party is expected to retain its dominant position.

Article Title: Second-year IIT-Bombay student dies by suicide after being caught using AI platform during exam
Article Text:
Students protest outside the IIT Bombay (Powai)

Poll Vote & Share your view Would you support a student-led initiative aimed at improving mental health resources on campus? Absolutely! No, I don't think it would help. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





MUMBAI: A second-year student of the Department of Energy Science and Engineering died by suicide at IIT-Bombay Friday evening. According to a statement shared by the institute, the student was found using a mobile phone in the exam hall during an examination, earlier in the day on Friday. He had uploaded the exam question paper on an AI platform to seek answers, it added.Students gathered in large numbers at the campus demanding a detailed probe into the circumstances that led to the suicide. The students alleged the authorities are not focusing on their mental health concerns.The institute’s statement said no disciplinary action was initiated against the student. “The matter was also discussed with the student by the instructor and the head of the department, who counselled him and assured him that the incident would not adversely affect his academic career,” mentioned the statement. It added that the student subsequently returned to his hostel room. Later in the evening, he was found dead in his room, it added.The institute, in the statement, said that they are deeply saddened by the loss of a student. “The institute is extending support to the student’s friends, classmates, faculty members, and others affected by this tragic incident. The circumstances surrounding the death are being looked into by the appropriate authorities,” it added.The police were in the process of recording the statements of students and faculty members at the time of going to press.On July 28, a 20-year-old second-year BTech student died by suicide in his single-occupancy room in the same hostel. Police found no suicide note but seized his phone. Investigators suspected a failed relationship after finding a notebook containing a half-page note about love failure and depression.
Article Summary: A second-year student of the Department of Energy Science and Engineering died by suicide at IIT-Bombay Friday evening. According to a statement shared by the institute, the student was found using a mobile phone in the exam hall during an examination. He had uploaded the exam question paper on an AI platform to seek answers, it added.

Article Title: Death toll mounts to 31 in suicide blast at Pakistan police compound, several still critical
Article Text:
Army soldiers examine the site following a powerful bomb exploded at a mosque in Kohat (AP photo)

Explosives-laden car hits mosque

Militants claim responsibility

The death toll from a suicide attack on a police compound in north-western Pakistan has risen to 31, news agency AFP reported on Saturday, citing a police official.The attack took place on Friday when an explosives-packed car was driven into the police facility as officers and their families were praying at a mosque inside the compound.Around 80 people, mostly police personnel, were taken to hospital after the blast. Several injured people were in critical condition, raising fears that the death toll could increase. The number of civilian casualties was not immediately known.The attacker drove a vehicle carrying explosives into the compound shortly after noon, striking the mosque's entrance wall. The blast brought part of the building down and left the area covered in smoke and debris.Officials believe three to five gunmen, in addition to the suicide attacker who drove the vehicle, may have tried to enter the compound. Witnesses reported gunfire as the attackers attempted to force their way inside.Among those killed were an SP-rank officer, a deputy SP and three inspectors from the Counter-Terrorism Department, according to sources.Videos shared on social media showed extensive damage at the site, with people fleeing the area as thick smoke rose from the compound.No group had officially claimed responsibility by late Friday. However, suspicion has fallen on Ittehad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, an umbrella alliance of three militant groups operating in the region.Another group, Inqilabi Islami Pakistan, which is affiliated with al-Qaida in the Indian subcontinent, also claimed responsibility for the attack on Telegram.Accounts supporting IMP said its Al Badr suicide unit carried out what they described as an ‘Ishtashadi operation’ at the Counter-Terrorism Department premises.Rescue teams continued clearing the site and searching for victims after the attack, while authorities assessed the full extent of the casualties.
Article Summary: Death toll from suicide attack on police compound in Kohat rises to 31. Around 80 people, mostly police personnel, were taken to hospital after the blast. Several injured people were in critical condition, raising fears that the death toll could increase. No group had officially claimed responsibility by late Friday.

Article Title: 9-year-old girl dies day after falling down school stairs in Telangana's Shadnagar
Article Text:
A nine-year-old girl named Varnika died Friday after a fall down school stairs (Picture credits: X)





HYDERABAD: A nine-year-old girl died on Friday, a day after she fell down a flight of stairs at her school in Shadnagar.According to Shadnagar CI K Seetharam, the incident occurred on Thursday when the girl, identified as Varnika, was reportedly descending the school stairs and lost her balance. She sustained serious injuries and was shifted to a nearby hospital by school staff. She died while undergoing treatment on Friday.CI Seetharam said no complaint had been lodged with the police as of Friday night. The officer also said Varnika reportedly had a pre-existing heart condition.The incident was captured on the school’s CCTV cameras. The footage reportedly showed Varnika losing her balance and falling while using the stairs.
Article Summary: The incident occurred on Thursday when the girl, identified as Varnika, was reportedly descending the school stairs. She sustained serious injuries and was shifted to a nearby hospital by school staff. She died while undergoing treatment on Friday. The incident was captured on the school’s CCTV cameras.

Article Title: Hugs, kisses minutes before Indian-origin woman and her friend get killed by train in Manhattan: Report
Article Text:
The operator attempted to stop the train but could not prevent the collision.

An Indian-origin woman may have jumped onto a New York City subway track in an attempt to rescue her friend after he ended up on the tracks, before both were fatally struck by an approaching train, according to a report by the New York Post citing law-enforcement sources.Malaika Chitre, 24, and her longtime friend Navam Kaul, also 24, were killed at the Spring Street subway station in Lower Manhattan at around 3.15am on Sunday. Both were recent graduates of Rutgers University and had recently begun their professional careers.According to the New York Post, Chitre and Kaul were seen hugging and kissing on the platform shortly before the incident. Kaul then appeared to lose his balance and fall onto the tracks, hitting his head, prompting Chitre to go down after him to help.Law-enforcement sources told the Post that it remained unclear whether Kaul fell or deliberately made his way onto the tracks. But investigators were examining the possibility that Chitre followed him in an attempt to pull him to safety.An incident report obtained by the New York Daily News said the train operator told supervisors that she saw Chitre and Kaul sitting on the tracks as a southbound No. 4 train entered the station.The operator attempted to stop the train but could not prevent the collision.The report said Chitre appeared to be laughing and pulling Kaul towards her when the train struck them. Video footage circulating on social media also appeared to show the pair sitting together on the tracks shortly before the train arrived.The train operator activated the emergency brake, but there was not enough time to stop, according to reports. About 100 passengers were later evacuated from the train.Investigators are also examining whether alcohol or drugs played a role and whether the pair may have been too impaired or disoriented to understand the danger. However, there has been no official finding that either was intoxicated.Suicide has also been considered, but investigators have not concluded that the deaths were intentional. The New York Post reported that no suicide note was found at the scene.Chitre, who was from South Brunswick, New Jersey, graduated from Rutgers with a degree in public health and was working as a quality operations specialist at Acadia Pharmaceuticals while pursuing a Doctor of Pharmacy degree at Temple University. Kaul, from Sayreville, graduated from Rutgers Business School with a degree in finance and worked as a financial data analyst at Bloomberg.The two were part of the same social circles and South Asian community around Rutgers and had remained close friends after graduating in 2024.
Article Summary: Malaika Chitre, 24, and her longtime friend Navam Kaul, also 24, were killed at the Spring Street subway station in Lower Manhattan at around 3.15am on Sunday. Both were recent graduates of Rutgers University and had recently begun their professional careers. Kaul appeared to lose his balance and fall onto the tracks, hitting his head, prompting Ch itre to go down after him to help.

Article Title: IIT-Bombay students protest overnight after 2nd-year student dies by suicide
Article Text:
Protests erupted on the IIT-Bombay campus after a student's death by suicide.





Fresh protests have been organised on the IIT-Bombay campus on Saturday morning as several students continued their demonstration through the night after a second-year student died by suicide. The student’s parents, who are from Yavatmal, reached the campus on Saturday.They called the incident as a case of casteism and 'institutional torture', claiming that their son would not have taken such an extreme step. They reportedly sought a CID inquiry into the matter and demanded action against officials they held responsible for their son’s death.Campus residents will be organising candlelight march later in the day and students plan to continue with the protest till some substantial action is taken.The student had been caught with a mobile phone during his exam on Friday. While students alleged that he was threatened with suspension, IIT-Bombay, in a statement issued on Friday night, said no disciplinary action was initiated against him. "The matter was also discussed with the student by the instructor and the head of the department, who counselled him and assured him that the incident would not adversely affect his academic career," mentioned the institute's statement.The mid-semester examinations scheduled for Saturday was postponed. An accidental death report was filed by the Powai police.The institute director, Shireesh Kedare, had an interaction with the students in the convocation hall in the early hours of Saturday. Students, however, continued with the protest near the main gate.During the protests, students demanded accountability and stronger mental health support on campus. They sought the resignation of the director, dean of student affairs and the exam invigilator who was on duty in the student’s class. They also demanded that an institutional task force be set up to address the incident and sought an independent inquiry into the last four student suicides, along with public disclosure of its findings.Students also called for compulsory mental-health sensitisation workshops for professors and sought measures to ensure the smooth functioning and accessibility of the institute’s wellness centres.
Article Summary: Second-year student had been caught with a mobile phone during his exam on Friday. Parents of the student, who is from Yavatmal, reached the campus on Saturday. They called the incident a case of casteism and 'institutional torture'

Article Title: Acquitted in Nithari case, Surinder Koli had two IDs — one in his own name and another as ‘Sada Ram’
Article Text:
The acquitted in the Nithari case, Surendra Koli died by suicide

Koli had two IDs, one in his own name, the other as Sada Ram





DEHRADUN: After spending nearly 19 years in prison and escaping gallows by a few hours, Surinder Koli , 53, who was once the prime accused in the infamous Nithari case , was found hanging inside his tea kiosk in Haridwar on Friday, barely five days after starting the business. Branded the "Nithari cannibal" in a case of gruesome killings of women and children that shocked the nation, Koli was acquitted by the Supreme Court last Nov, and was now living as a "free man".Police said to hide his past, Koli was probably using a "different name" in Haridwar since most of the locals knew him as "Sada Ram". After his death, police recovered his Aadhaar card which revealed his real name.On Friday morning, customers who frequented his kiosk found it shut. "They peeped inside and found him hanging from a noose. Prima facie, it seems to be a case of suicide," said circle officer, Haridwar Shishupal Singh Negi. A panel of doctors will carry out the postmortem.No suicide note was found either on him or inside the kiosk, he said.For two decades, Koli, a Dalit from Mangaru Khal village in Uttarakhand's Almora district, who worked as a domestic help at the house of Noida-based businessman Moninder Singh Pandher, was a branded man.He was accused of being a "cannibal" who would allegedly lure children to Pandher's house, murder them, and "eat their flesh". On Dec 29, 2006, Koli and Pandher were arrested.But after a long legal battle lasting two decades and 13 death sentences later, SC, on Nov 11, passed an acquittal order in the last of the 13th cases against Koli. Two days later, he walked out a free man from Greater Noida's Luksar Jail.A few months ago, he landed in Haridwar where he had recently taken up a kiosk on a monthly rent of Rs 6,000 using his voter ID card as a validating document since it bore the name 'Sada Ram'. Prior to that, Koli was working as a security guard in Sidcul area of the town.He had worked for around 10 days as a guard but he left that job after the employers asked for his Aadhaar card. Cops have now found both the voter ID and his Aadhaar -which bore the name 'Surinder Koli' along with his Noida address. Police and the locals came to know his real identity from his Aadhaar.Almora-based social activist Narayan Singh Rawat, who had helped his family during the trials, said he suspects Koli's death to be "murder". Rawat, who hails from Almora's Salt area, had helped the family monetarily and facilitated Koli's meeting with his mother in prison."I was in regular touch with him and had recently lent him Rs 25,000 to start a tea kiosk, which he had taken on rent from a local resident linked to a political outfit. Over the phone (in the past 2-3 days), he complained of harassment. They're asking for more money, he told me... He sounded disturbed and couldn't figure out a solution," Rawat told TOI.Koli is survived by his wife, daughter and a teenaged son. His wife had started living at a relative's place in Haryana, along with their children, when he was arrested in the case in 2006. Later his wife got married again. His daughter, who was in her 20s at the time of his release from jail last year, also got married a few years ago. His mother had passed away in 2022. Among the siblings, his elder brother lives in Delhi, while his younger brother lives in Almora with his family.The younger brother told TOI, "I was in regular touch with my brother over the phone. But he never shared anything that was bothering him. We're unaware of the reason behind his suicide, as claimed by police."
Article Summary: Surinder Koli, 53, was found hanging inside his tea kiosk in Haridwar on Friday. He was acquitted by the Supreme Court last Nov, and was now living as a "free man" Police said to hide his past, Koli was probably using a "different name" Most of the locals knew him as "Sada Ram"

Article Title: Eknath Shinde’s phone left behind on UK flight recovered in an hour
Article Text:
Maharashtra Deputy CM Eknath Shinde





MUMBAI: DCM Eknath Sh­i­nde left his iPhone behind on a London Mumbai flight early Friday, leading to a frantic search. The phone, however, was retrieved by police in an hour from the British Airways flight and returned to him.Shinde was on a two-day visit to London starting Sep 5, and received the Commonw­ealth Leadership award and the Statesmanship award in the UK Parliament. Shinde’s plane landed at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport at 2am. After reaching home at 3 am, Shinde noticed that his mobile phone was missing.The police in his security detail were immediately informed.
Article Summary: Shinde was on a two-day visit to London starting Sep 5, and received the Commonw­ealth Leadership award and the Statesmanship award in the UK Parliament. His plane landed at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport at 2am. After reaching home at 3am, Shinde noticed that his mobile phone was missing.

Article Title: Out on bail, old enmity, 3-4 men in car: How pregnant YouTuber wife’s murder accused was hacked to death
Article Text:
Chithari Haribabu, recently released on bail, was hacked to death by unknown assailants.

'Old enmity'





HYDERABAD: About six months after he was arrested for allegedly killing his pregnant wife, who was also a YouTuber, Chithari Haribabu was hacked to death by a group of unidentified men at Rajarajendra (RR) Centre in Nizamabad on Thursday. He had been out on bail for the past two months.According to B Prasad, ACP, Nizamabad, 26-year-old Haribabu was intercepted by a group of men in a car near Rajarajendra Chowrasta at around 5pm. "Three to four people arrived in a car. One person got out, followed Haribabu and attacked him on the neck and head with a knife used for cutting coconuts," the ACP said. The victim suffered severe injuries and died on the spot. His body was shifted to the govt general hospital, Nizamabad, for postmortem.While police suspect old enmity to be the motive, they have launched an investigation to ascertain the facts. Investigators are also examining whether Haribabu's killing was linked to the murder of his wife, Vaishnavi. On March 17, Vaishnavi, who ran a popular YouTube channel, 'Vaishu Amma', was found dead at her residence in Madhapur village of Korutla mandal, Jagtial, when she was four months pregnant.Her family alleged that Haribabu strangled her and attacked her with a knife following a heated argument between them the previous night. Based on a complaint by Vaishnavi's father, police registered a murder case and arrested Haribabu after taking him into custody on the outskirts of Korutla.Police also booked his mother, Lakshmi, and brothers, Anand and Ashok, for alleged dowry harassment. Haribabu was subsequently released on bail in July."We suspect Vaishnavi's brothers' involvement in this murder but are yet to establish it. We have booked a murder case and are probing all angles to establish the identity of the accused," the ACP added.
Article Summary: Chithari Haribabu, 26, was hacked to death by a group of unidentified men. He had been out on bail for the past two months after being arrested for allegedly killing his pregnant wife, who was also a YouTuber. Police suspect old enmity to be the motive.

Article Title: Apple manager’s murder: 8 years on, 1 cop convicted, another let off
Article Text:
vivek tiwari murder by up police constable at saheed path gomti nagar , residence of vivek tiwari at new hyderabad aakash ganga hospital police constable and other people are gatherd at there residence

Daughters struggle to cope with father’s death

Dissatisfied with verdict, will appeal in higher court: Vivek’s wife





LUCKNOW: Eight years after a 38-year-old Apple area sales manager Vivek Tiwari was allegedly shot dead by two cops in Lucknow, a local court on Thursday convicted constable Prashant Chaudhary of culpable homicide not amounting to murder, while acquitting co-accused constable Sandeep Kumar . The quantum of punishment will be announced on Sept 21.District/sessions judge Malkhan Singh held Prashant Chaudhary guilty under the charges of IPC 304 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder).As per police chargesheet, Prashant was accused of IPC 302 (murder) and co-accused Sandeep of IPC 323 (voluntarily causing hurt).Soon after the judgement was pronounced, both the cops and their kin erupted in joy.Pranshu Agarwal, who represented Vivek Tiwar’s family, told TOI they will go through the detailed judgement and then file an appeal in the high court. “We are awaiting for the judgement copy in the case and also pronouncement of judgement on Sep 21,” said Agarwal.Vivek Tiwari, a resident of New Hyderabad colony, was driving his former colleague Sana Siddiqui to her home in his XUV around 1:30am on Sept 29, 2018. As they reached near Makdoompur outpost in Gomti Nagar Extension, bike-borne cops Prashant Chaudhary and Sandeep signalled them to stop.As Sana lowered the window pane to enquire about the reason, Sandeep hit her with a baton.Vivek did not stop and kept driving. At this, Prashant allegedly took out his service pistol and shot at Vivek, who had barely driven 0.5km ahead.The bullet hit Vivek and he rammed the vehicle on a divider. The two cops fled. Sana sought help from the police control room and took Vivek to Lohia Hospital where he died during treatment.An FIR against the two cops was lodged the next day and the chargesheet against them was filed on Dec 19, 2018. Prashant was charged with murder, while Sandeep was initially charged under Section 323.Vivek’s daughters, aged 15 and 20, still go numb on the mention of his tragic demise. Divyanshi, who was just 7 at the time of incident, had initially been told that her dad was away in Delhi and would return soon. But now the teen girl knows the reality. Priyanshi tries to console her younger sibling every time she breaks down. Divyanshi’s favourite possession is a family drawing she made years ago depicting Vivek, Kalpana, Priyanshi, and herself.Vivek wife Kalpana’s life has been consumed by grief. Every corner of her home is filled with memories of her husband. As she steps into her role as Officer on Special Duty at Nagar Nigam, she carries the weight of her husband’s absence. Kalpana’s brother, Vishnu, said, “He was always there for us, guiding us, helping us. Now, all we want is justice.”Kalpana Tiwari expressed strong dissatisfaction with the verdict and said she would challenge it before a higher court. Speaking after the judgment, she described the decision as disappointing and said the family had expected a harsher punishment.“We had been waiting for the court’s decision since morning and hoped that justice would be delivered. But we are disappointed with the verdict,” Kalpana said, according to the report. She questioned how a trained police constable could have made a mistake while firing his service weapon and maintained that her husband had been shot dead. Kalpana also questioned Sandeep Kumar’s acquittal, saying both constables were present at the spot and, in her view, shared responsibility for the incident.
Article Summary: Vivek Tiwari, 38, was driving his former colleague Sana Siddiqui to her home in his XUV around 1:30am on Sept 29, 2018. As they reached near Makdoompur outpost in Gomti Nagar Extension, bike-borne cops Prashant Chaudhary and Sandeep signalled them to stop. As Sana lowered the window pane to enquire about the reason, Sandeeps hit her with a baton. Vivek did not stop and kept driving.

Article Title: 'Ab nikaal ke bata gadi': A month before Gurgaon hit-and-run case, men chased, harassed Bhopal biker
Article Text:
In Bhopal, biker Abida Rana encountered a troubling situation when two men in a car relentlessly pursued her on Nabibagh Road





BHOPAL: Nearly a month before a woman biker’s hit-and-run incident in Gurgaon sparked widespread outrage, 23-year-old Bhopal-based biker, Abida Rana, had faced a similar ordeal in the city, with two men in a car chasing her for around 600-700 metres, abusing and repeatedly blocking her way.The ordeal took place on Aug 2 on Nabibagh Road, under Nishatpura police station limits. Abida had shared a video of the Bhopal ordeal on her Instagram handle on Aug 5, which is being widely circulated now.According to Abida, she was around 5 km from home when on the Nishatpura-Nabibagh stretch, two men crossing the road allegedly stopped their car in the middle of the road near the divider and began abusing her without any apparent reason.One of the men allegedly shouted, “Ab nikaal ke bata gadi.” With vehicles behind her honking, Abida said she was forced to move around the car from the left side.The men allegedly changed course and started following her, and repeatedly blocking her way.Abida said she became panicked and angry and told the men that the police station was only 1-2 km away and warned them that she would complain if they continued following and threatening her.When she tried to drive away, the men allegedly blocked her path from the right side as well. She then drove towards the police station, claiming the men continued chasing her and hurling abuses. They left just before the police station.Later, the men were called up to the police station and cops warned the men not to approach her again and made them write an apology before allowing them to leave. No FIR was registered as Abida had opted not to pursue a criminal case, cops said.
Article Summary: Bhopal-based biker Abida Rana, 23, faced a similar ordeal in the city. Two men in a car chased her for around 600-700 metres, abusing and repeatedly blocking her way. Abida had shared a video of the Bhopal ordeal on her Instagram handle.

Article Title: Abandoned pony limping through Kharagpur traffic rescued for veterinary care
Article Text:
A rescued pony, previously abandoned and struggling with severe health issues, was saved from the bustling traffic in Kharagpur





KHARAGPUR: A 7- to 8-year-old skewbald pony found limping through traffic on Kharagpur’s Malancha Road with severely overgrown hooves and other painful health conditions has been rescued and transported to an Animal Rahat sanctuary for veterinary care and rehabilitation. The rescue was carried out following action by People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals India (PETA India), with assistance from West Midnapore district magistrate Bijin Krishna; Superintendent of Police Papiya Sultana; Kharagpur sub-divisional officer Bhuvana Pranith Pappula; Kharagpur Animal Resources Development department deputy director Chinmoy Chakraborty; Kharagpur Town Police Station inspector-in charge Amit Kumar Mitra; and local animal advocate Sudebi Bhattacharya. The operation also received support from Members of Parliament June Maliah and Sayani Ghosh.The abandoned pony was suffering from severely overgrown and enlarged hooves, swollen fetlock joints, chronic osteoarthritis, and impaired mobility. Despite the animal’s evident distress, PETA India personnel faced resistance from certain locals, delaying rescue efforts. The pony was finally secured and taken for treatment after intervention by local authorities and the MPs.“This abandoned pony is yet another victim of the joyride industry. This rescue shows what can be achieved when authorities, animal protection groups, and citizens act together,” said Maliah. “I thank PETA India for never giving up on this pony and Animal Rahat for housing the pony and all the officials led by DM Bijin Krishna and SP Sultana for their prompt intervention in the rescue operation. I urge the public to help other ponies by choosing animal-free forms of entertainment. ”In Kolkata, PETA India continues to campaign for the protection of horses used to haul tourist carriages. In June 2026 alone, the group registered three FIRs involving neglected or distressed horses, including a foal found running frantically through active traffic, a horse with severely overgrown hooves rescued from the Hastings area, and a mare who died in the middle of traffic in Ekbalpore. Since 2024, at least 18 horses in the city have reportedly died or succumbed to injuries from road accidents and other causes.The Calcutta High Court has taken note of the poor condition of horses, the prevalence of unlicensed hackney carriages, and the abandonment of ailing animals. In an order dated May 9, 2024, it directed the state government to develop a proposal to rehabilitate horse-carriage owners so that replacing horse-drawn carriages, as done in Mumbai, can be considered. On July 7, 2026, PETA India appealed for horse-drawn tourist carriages in Kolkata to be replaced with heritage-style electric carriages.PETA India, whose motto reads in part that “animals are not ours to use for entertainment,” opposes speciesism, a human-supremacist worldview.
Article Summary: A 7- to 8-year-old skewbald pony was found limping through traffic on Kharagpur’s Malancha Road. The pony was suffering from severely overgrown and enlarged hooves, swollen fetlock joints, chronic osteoarthritis, and impaired mobility. The rescue was carried out following action by People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals India.

Article Title: Woman dies by suicide; family cites online gaming losses and emotional distress in UP
Article Text:
A 38-year-old woman died by suicide at her Lucknow residence on Wednesday evening (AI image)





LUCKNOW: A 38-year-old woman died by suicide at her residence in Sushant Golf City area on Wednesday evening, with her family attributing the death to severe emotional distress following losses linked to online gaming and the alleged pledging of jewellery without their knowledge.The woman, identified as Vibha Gupta, a resident of Patel Nagar, was found unresponsive inside a room of the house.Inspector Rajeev Ranjan Upadhyay said Vibha’s husband, Rajkumar Gupta , told investigators that she had developed an addiction to online gaming and had lost a substantial amount of money while playing. Family members also informed police that Vibha had allegedly pledged some of her jewellery without informing them. After Rajkumar learned about the financial losses and the jewellery being pledged, he asked her to stop playing online games, they said.According to the family, Vibha remained deeply distressed in the aftermath of the financial losses and related tensions. Police said Rajkumar and Vibha were at home when the incident occurred.Rajkumar, a retired Army personnel, is currently working as a head clerk at Bank of Baroda in Vibhuti Khand. Police recorded statements from family members and are collecting relevant information as part of the inquiry.Family members said Rajkumar was previously married to Sunita Gupta, who died during treatment at Command Hospital in 2000. He has two daughters from the first marriage, Khushboo and Nikki. Rajkumar married Vibha in 2004, and the couple have a 17-year-old son, Atharva.
Article Summary: The woman, identified as Vibha Gupta, a resident of Patel Nagar, was found unresponsive inside a room of the house. Her husband, Rajkumar Gupta, told investigators that she had developed an addiction to online gaming and had lost a substantial amount of money while playing. Family members also informed police that Vibia had allegedly pledged some of her jewellery without informing them.

Article Title: ‘They’re my family’: Bengaluru woman stops crowd from attacking men accused of kidnapping her
Article Text:
Locals attacked a car on Magadi Road, suspecting a kidnapping attempt





BENGALURU: High drama unfolded on Magadi Road Wednesday night after a group of locals allegedly thrashed several men and damaged their car, suspecting they were trying to kidnap a young woman.Six persons, including a nine-year-old girl, sustained injuries in the commotion.However, the alleged kidnapping took a dramatic turn when the woman intervened and told the crowd that the men were her own family members, including her father, who had come from Rajasthan to take her back home.Speaking to police who arrived at the spot, the woman said she had married a man from another caste despite her family’s opposition. She alleged that her family had recently traced her to Bengaluru and was trying to force her to return to Rajasthan.“I’ve married a man from another caste and my family was against it. Recently, we came here and my family somehow followed me,” she told police.A senior police officer said the woman was being requested to lodge a complaint against her family so that action could be taken.Meanwhile, the family’s vehicle was badly damaged after the crowd attacked it. The family members allegedly tried to flee the spot, ramming into other vehicles in the process, officials added.Of those injured, one woman with serious head injuries has been shifted to the ICU of a nearby private hospital, police added. Cops said they are yet to register a case. Suspects have been detained and the car used in the “kidnapping” seized, police said.
Article Summary: Six persons, including a nine-year-old girl, sustained injuries in the commotion. The woman said she had married a man from another caste despite her family’s opposition. She alleged that her family had recently traced her to Bengaluru and was trying to force her to return to Rajasthan.

Article Title: Urinal in food storage area: Mumbai's iconic Olympia Coffee House loses licence
Article Text:
Olympia Coffee House in Colaba had its food licence suspended due to hygiene violations
